A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the accumulation of the exogeneous transmitter is inhibited in the tissue and adrenergic nerve terminals when the NE content in the tissue reaches a certain critical value (i.e. when the tissue contains more than 90% of the total transmitter reserves) and the antidepressants and cholinolytics are present in the medium.

the accumulation of exogenous NE in adrenergic nerve endings is a process that can be influenced by antidepressants and by the cholinolytics.
